description:
We are seeking an exceptionally talented and entrepreneurial AI engineer to build next-generation Artificial Intelligence capabilities that transform how scientific knowledge is accessed, interpreted, synthesized, and applied across global R&D.
 This is a fast-moving, highly exploratory role within the Materials Science & Characterization (MSC) organization, operating as an AI skunk works focused on developing custom AI systems and intelligent applications for scientific and engineering challenges.
 The successful candidate will work at the intersection of advanced AI architectures, large language models (LLMs), information retrieval, knowledge engineering, and scientific computing. A central part of the mission will be to develop sophisticated Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures that connect LLMs to proprietary scientific databases, experimental datasets, technical literature, patents, and internal knowledge repositories.
 Beyond conventional LLM applications, the candidate will explore and build custom solutions using LLMs, multimodal language models, and small language models (SLMs), along with agentic architectures capable of reasoning, retrieving information, orchestrating computational tools, and executing complex scientific workflows.
 We are looking for someone who thrives on experimentation, moves rapidly from concepts to working prototypes, and has the technical depth to build custom AI solutions rather than simply assemble existing tools. The opportunity is to establish entirely new ways of leveraging scientific knowledge and computational intelligence to accelerate innovation.
 Key Responsibilities
 Advanced LLM and RAG Architectures
 Design, develop, and implement advanced RAG architectures connecting LLMs to complex scientific and engineering databases.

 Explore and develop hybrid, graph-based, hierarchical, multimodal, and agentic RAG approaches.

 Build sophisticated retrieval, reranking, embedding, and context-engineering pipelines to improve accuracy, relevance, and scientific grounding.

 Develop mechanisms for source attribution, traceability, provenance, and reliable retrieval of scientific information.

 Integrate structured and unstructured data sources, including scientific databases, technical reports, patents, publications, experimental datasets, and engineering documentation.

 Custom AI Models and Intelligent Agents
 Develop, fine-tune, adapt, and deploy custom LLMs, multimodal models, and SLMs for specialized scientific and engineering applications.

 Build agentic AI systems capable of multi-step reasoning, information retrieval, data analysis, and computational task execution.

 Develop multi-agent architectures that coordinate specialized tools, models, and scientific workflows.

 Explore emerging model architectures, orchestration frameworks, and AI development paradigms to identify opportunities for competitive differentiation.

 Evaluate open-source and commercial foundation models and determine optimal architectures for specific scientific applications.

 Scientific Knowledge Engineering
 Develop intelligent interfaces and knowledge systems that make complex scientific databases accessible through natural language and semantic search.

 Build knowledge graphs, scientific ontologies, and semantic representations connecting materials, formulations, processes, structures, properties, and performance.

 Develop pipelines for extracting and structuring scientific information from heterogeneous sources, including complex documents, tables, figures, and experimental records.

 Establish robust approaches for data preparation, indexing, metadata management, and continuous knowledge integration.

 AI Application Development and Rapid Prototyping
 Rapidly conceptualize, prototype, and demonstrate novel AI applications addressing high-value scientific and engineering challenges.

 Develop custom AI tools and applications using modern software engineering, model orchestration, and deployment frameworks.

 Integrate LLMs with scientific databases, Python-based computational tools, simulation platforms, and analytical workflows.

 Explore emerging technologies and translate promising concepts into practical, working applications.

 Establish evaluation frameworks to assess model accuracy, retrieval quality, hallucination rates, reliability, security, and practical utility.

 Collaboration and Innovation Across R&D
 Work closely with materials scientists, computational scientists, experimentalists, and engineers to identify opportunities for AI-enabled scientific discovery.

 Translate complex scientific problems into computational architectures and working AI solutions.

 Help establish new capabilities and technical standards for the responsible deployment of AI across R&D.

 Stay at the forefront of developments in LLMs, agentic AI, multimodal systems, and scientific AI.

 
 BS or MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related technical discipline.

 Candidates from engineering disciplines will also be considered with exceptional computer science foundations and demonstrated AI engineering expertise.

 Strong programming and software development skills, particularly in Python.

 Demonstrated experience developing and implementing LLM-based applications, including RAG architectures.

 Strong understanding of modern machine learning, deep learning, transformer architectures, embeddings, vector databases, and information retrieval.

 Experience with modern AI development frameworks and tools, such as PyTorch, Hugging Face, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or equivalent technologies.

 Experience working with APIs, databases, data pipelines, and software integration.

 Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to translate ambiguous problems into practical computational solutions.

 Ability to work independently as well as in a diverse cross-functional team, experiment rapidly, and develop working prototypes with minimal supervision.

 Experience in one or more of the following areas is highly desirable:
 Advanced RAG architectures, including Graph RAG, Agentic RAG, and multimodal RAG.

 Fine-tuning and customization of open-source LLMs and SLMs.

 Multi-agent systems and intelligent AI orchestration.

 Knowledge graphs, ontologies, semantic search, and scientific knowledge representation.

 Vector databases and hybrid retrieval architectures.

 Model evaluation, benchmarking, and optimization.

 Multimodal AI involving technical documents, scientific images, tables, and structured/unstructured data.

 AI application development, deployment, and scalable software architectures.

 Integration of AI systems with scientific computing, simulation, and engineering tools. Experience in scientific, engineering, or industrial applications is particularly valuable.

 
 Less than 10% travel expected.

 
 All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, protected veteran status, or other protected status. EEOE/M/F/Vet/Disabled. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

As part of our commitment to maintaining a safe and productive work environment, Avery Dennison requires all final candidates to successfully complete a comprehensive background check and a drug screening. These checks are conducted post-offer and are a condition of employment. All results will be considered in accordance with applicable local, state, and federal laws.
